claims.statement: Talon defines a common ChannelAdapter protocol for lifecycle, host message-handler registration, text/media send and edit, typing, and status; ChannelMessage and ChannelReaction carry channel-specific conversation and sender identity plus metadata, while reactions are an optional adapter capability.

Shared ChannelExposure defaults to self, where from_self or configured operator IDs are admitted; allowlist admits configured conversation IDs or text glob patterns; open admits every message but configuration requires an explicit risk acknowledgement and logs the arbitrary-sender risk.

Pairing persists provider-scoped pending and approved records in a private atomic store: mutations are locked and atomically replaced, cache identity includes inode, unreadable or invalid state fails closed for paired access, and request codes are one-hour, single-use approvals.

Outbound channel media is constrained to a configured trusted root and validated for resolved path containment, regular-file existence, requested versus inferred type, and optional byte cap; this validation is a transport boundary rather than sender authorization or runtime containment.

Sender pairing is opt-in for Discord, Slack, and Telegram, excluded for WhatsApp, and invalid with open exposure. Discord and Telegram issue requests only from direct/private messages, whereas Slack can open a rejected non-DM sender's DM to offer and bind a request.

Once approved, a paired sender is admitted to messages and reactions in any chat visible to the adapter; the recorded DM is retained for pairing communications and legacy job matching rather than limiting post-approval access.

Pairing grants normal sender invocation but never operator authority: environment-configured operator and allowlisted IDs remain authoritative DM senders, while /pair is handled outside the model and requires an explicitly configured operator; pairing administration is DM-only except that an operator may approve a code outside a DM.

When an operator revokes a paired sender through the host, Talon cancels active work in the recorded DM and every tracked conversation that sender started, pauses the sender's provider-scoped cron jobs, and converts cancellation of an in-progress scheduled run into a revoked-run failure.

After adapter admission, TalonHost derives a provider-qualified conversation root and agent conversation ID, serializes work per root, replaces an active turn with a newer one, and treats adapter metadata as request context while retaining host control of the request conversation and selected model.

Discord drops self-authored gateway messages before turn and exposure checks; Slack preserves a root message's thread conversation ID and checks slash-command authorization before command discovery, with commands DM-only except operator /pair approve; Telegram applies pairing after normal admission fails.

Adapter admission of a reaction is not sufficient to resolve tool approval: the host requires a pending provider-qualified approval and checks reaction provider, conversation, prompt message, sender, and decision emoji before it settles the request.

The host routes result text and extracted markdown media references back to the origin conversation, retries transient send failures with exponential backoff, and suppresses stale turn results using the conversation generation.

The `deepagents-talon pairing` CLI can list and approve provider-scoped requests, revoke an approved sender, and pause that sender's jobs only while Talon is stopped; unlike host-mediated revocation, CLI store changes do not cancel work held by a running host.

TalonHost starts the runtime before channels, binds host callbacks before starting each channel, unwinds a partial startup in reverse order, and on shutdown cancels host work before stopping channels, scheduler, and runtime.

Talon roots each agent conversation in a trusted provider key plus adapter conversation ID, making that root the LangGraph thread and persisted reset key; a root can have a separate history scope, and public Discord threads retain thread-specific agent identity while sharing their numeric parent channel as history_chat.

MCP authorization callbacks are intercepted before model invocation and can complete a pending authorization only when provider, channel conversation, initiating sender, expected callback endpoint, and expiry all match the host's recorded binding.

After sender admission, Discord, Slack, and Telegram normalize downloaded inbound attachments into shared media metadata and preserve a message with an explicit media error when preparation fails; WhatsApp receives bridge-provided paths and filters existing over-cap files while retaining paths that may still be downloading.

When replacing or stopping an active channel turn, the host increments its generation, cancels it, and attempts runtime recovery within 30 seconds. A timeout blocks further work for that agent conversation, while stale or cancelled undelivered turns requeue consumed background-subagent results.

Discord requires guild messages to mention the bot or its integration role unless a configured mention-optional channel permits a human message; only after admission does a top-level guild turn open a public thread, with fallback to replying in the parent channel if thread creation fails.

Discord application-command interactions are converted to the typed command's ChannelMessage and pass the same admission check; admitted interactions are deferred and receive host output through a task-local follow-up sink, preventing concurrent work from being captured by the wrong interaction.

For admitted existing Discord guild-thread turns, Talon supplies bounded preceding context after its last bot reply, filtering it by trusted senders unless explicitly configured otherwise, excluding OAuth callbacks, labeling other bots as input data, and wrapping it in the host as context rather than instructions.

A shared command registry supplies host-visible command definitions, help text, and the visible Discord application-command set; hidden commands are still accepted when typed but are excluded from help and platform registration.
Talon derives a validated, assistant-namespaced home and creates its state directories with owner-only permissions; internal state paths are checked to remain inside that home.

`DEEPAGENTS_TALON_VERBOSITY` is validated per Talon assistant process as 1, 2, or 3 with default 1: level 1 omits the interim `send_message` tool, level 2 permits two invocation-local interim updates, and level 3 has no fixed interim-update budget; final replies and host-visible activity are separate from this setting.
